import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a count plot for the top 10 most common dog breeds
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10).index
breed_counts = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)]['Rasse1Text'].value_counts()

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(x=breed_counts.values, y=breed_counts.index, palette="viridis")
plt.title('Top 10 Most Common Dog Breeds in Zurich')
plt.xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs')
plt.ylabel('Dog Breed')
plt.gca().invert_yaxis()  # Invert y-axis to have the most common at the top

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a count plot for the top 10 most common dog breeds
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10).index
breed_counts = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)]['Rasse1Text'].value_counts()

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(x=breed_counts.values, y=breed_counts.index, palette="viridis")
plt.title('Top 10 Most Common Dog Breeds in Zurich')
plt.xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs')
plt.ylabel('Dog Breed')
plt.gca().invert_yaxis()  # Invert y-axis to have the most common at the top

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
